newsitem.title: USA: Nuveen sees 'soft landing' for utility players.
newsitem.headline: Nuveen sees 'soft landing' for utility players.

text.p: Utility bondholders are in for a bumpy ride as electricity deregulation sweeps through the Northeast, but in the end they "should have a soft landing," the head of research for John Nuveen & Co Inc said.

The Chicago-based mutual fund company's latest reports on New England utilities show most, including Boston Edison Co, New England Electric Systems and Northeast Utilities have negative outlooks for the bond ratings.

Paul Williams, Nuveen's vice president and manager of its research division, acknowledged in an interview that there has been a systematic erosion "in the perceived quality, the rating quality of the debt, thinner margins of coverage, but our view is that the credit jeopardy will be very, very rare."
Deregulation "is going to be bouncy, bumpy...but for most participants it will be a soft landing," he said. "This could be an opportunity."
But quality long-term utility credits are beginning to dry up.

Nuveen's John Hoeting, who specializes in utilities, noted that a recent offering for Virginia Power & Light, a subsidiary of Dominion Resources Inc "is issued through (20)22 but really its callable after five years. It's hard in this market to stay diversified. None of the utilities want to go out for 30 years of debt.
"Most of the credits that are offered are on the secondary market - and you have to look at those quite carefully," Hoeting added
Independent power producers and non-utility generators "here and there could run into some real problems," he said"
Meanwhile, the Massachusetts legislature is scheduled to hold hearings later Wednesday on its plan to deregulate the state's utilities.
The measure, which unlike a similar proposal offered by Gov. William Weld, mandates a 10 percent rate cut for consumers by Jan 1, 1998.

It would also allow utilities to recover 100 percent of stranded costs, estimated at $8.9 billion in Massachusetts, only after the utilities renegotiated contracts and attempted to sell-off those assets.
